scope: MIDI recording: PipeWire MIDI input, MidiTake note pairing, and desktop MIDI takes as piano-roll clips
environment: Kvant, pinned CI image (Qt 6.12, PipeWire 1.6.9), docker --network none, QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen, owned private PipeWire server at quantum 256, pw-midiplay as the independent source

measurements.reference file: 8 notes at 120 BPM, 96 PPQ (250 frames per tick): chord, overlaps, adjacent repeats, velocities 1..127

verified_behaviors: fl-live-midi-input receives every note of an independently authored SMF with exact frame timing relative to the first note

MidiTake pairs notes, treats velocity 0 as note-off, closes a held note on a repeated note-on and at the end, ignores other messages, counts overflow, and its callback neither allocates nor touches files
An armed MIDI track's take becomes the selected piano-roll clip with every note at its exact tick, length, pitch and mapped velocity
Recorded MIDI clips survive Undo/Redo and save/reopen and play when launched; a take without notes adds no clip; audio plus MIDI is one Undo step
limits: Private software graph and offscreen QML; no hardware MIDI controller, input monitoring, in-app input choice or latency compensation (#45). MIDI takes are held in memory and are not recoverable after a crash. Tick quantization at the session tempo is the stated policy, not a measured placement against the transport.
